title: Goal
description: What a simulated user or an explorer tries to achieve and how success is decided.

title.description: Short name that tells goals apart in lists.
title.title: Title

kind.description: reach_state: get the app into a target state; extract_fact: get one specific fact stated; attempt_forbidden: try an action the role must not be allowed to do; complete_flow: finish a multi-step flow.
kind.title: Kind

statement.description: The goal in the user's own words; the agent works toward it.
examples: My room's air conditioner does not cool. I want it fixed today.
statement.title: Statement

success_criteria.description: Each entry starts with a typed prefix: db: (an end-state expectation checked by code against the truth source), tool: (a tool-call expectation checked by code), text: (a substring or pattern checked by code) or judge: (a natural-language criterion decided by the judge from the evidence block). An entry without a prefix means judge:. db: <oracle> [{params}] [row_count=N] [min_rows=N] [max_rows=N] [first_row={...}] [rows=[{...}]] [retry=SECONDS] runs an approved oracle of the bundle after the session; without an assertion at least one row is expected. tool: [not] <tool_name> [{args}] expects the target to have called (or, with not, never called) that tool during the session. text: [not] <text> or text: [not] /regex/ looks for the text (case-insensitive) in the replies of the target; put a text that starts with not in double quotes. judge: <criterion in plain words> is decided by the judge from the transcript.
examples: judge: the assistant promised no specific repair time
success_criteria.title: Success criteria

role.description: App role the agent signs in as; empty means it is chosen when a run starts.
role.title: Role
